project_name: Gemello Digitale Civico (Bologna Civic Digital Twin)
lead_institutions: Municipality of Bologna, Fondazione Innovazione Urbana (FIU), University of Bologna, Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK)
governance_model: Participatory Neighborhood Labs (Laboratori di quartiere) & Public Data Commons
hard_data_layers: Satellite thermal imaging, urban tree canopy GIS, mobility flows, building energy profiles
soft_civic_layers: Neighborhood social vulnerability surveys, citizen co-design assemblies, lived heat-stress reporting
primary_civic_application: Climate neutrality by 2030: simulating placement of 'green cooling cells' and pedestrian zones in working-class urban heat islands rather than commercial corridors.
key_democratic_safeguard: Legally frames the digital twin as a democratic commons where neighborhood assembly feedback modifies simulation weights.

lead_institutions: Barcelona City Council, Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC), Decidim Free Software Association
hard_data_layers: Multi-modal traffic telemetry, acoustic noise sensors, NO2 air quality grids, parcel land-use data
soft_civic_layers: Decidim citizen proposals, neighborhood demographic vulnerability, eldercare & school walkability surveys
primary_civic_application: Superblocks (Superilles) spillover modeling and 15-Minute City spatial equity audits for low-income neighborhoods.
key_democratic_safeguard: 100% open-source software stack preventing Big Tech cloud lock-in and proprietary vendor enclosure.

lead_institutions: City of Helsinki, Forum Virium Helsinki
governance_model: Open Semantic 3D Commons (CityGML + Open Mesh) & District Co-Design Sandbox
hard_data_layers: CityGML semantic 3D model, high-resolution photogrammetry mesh, BIM architectural permitting files, wind/solar simulations
soft_civic_layers: Browser-based resident 3D annotations, VR public space walkthrough feedback, local school/park usage diaries
primary_civic_application: Kalasatama district co-design: residents walked through proposed parks, transit stops, and building massing in VR/browser before construction.
key_democratic_safeguard: Open-access municipal data license allowing independent civic groups and residents to inspect BIM proposals before permits are issued.

lead_institutions: City of Gothenburg, Chalmers University of Technology, EU DigiTwins4PEDs Consortium
governance_model: Public Dialogue Portal & Positive Energy District Co-Creation
hard_data_layers: 400-km2 high-resolution 3D topographic twin, building retrofit energy models, solar irradiance maps
soft_civic_layers: Geolocated citizen pins on MinStad (perceived night-time safety, lived memories, community garden proposals)
primary_civic_application: Bridging qualitative neighborhood safety perceptions with multi-stakeholder urban decarbonization roadmaps.
key_democratic_safeguard: Direct public write-access to the spatial map layer via MinStad without requiring GIS technical expertise.

project_name: Smart Docklands & Dublin Community Digital Twin
lead_institutions: Dublin City Council, Trinity College Dublin, Connect Centre
hard_data_layers: 3D building massing, shadow/daylight trajectories, wind-tunneling CFD, River Liffey coastal flood models
soft_civic_layers: Working-class resident workshops, AR street-level visualizations, community amenity displacement audits
primary_civic_application: Empowering working-class Docklands residents to evaluate shadow, wind, and displacement impacts of adjacent Big Tech campus high-rises.
key_democratic_safeguard: Translates complex architectural environmental impact filings into mobile AR views verifiable at the street corner.

lead_institutions: City of Zurich Open Data, ETH Zurich (MATSim)
hard_data_layers: Agent-based transit micro-simulations (MATSim), pedestrian zoning models, urban micro-climate layers
soft_civic_layers: Public consultation scenarios, municipal referendum voter information packets, commuter diaries
primary_civic_application: Feeding transparent 'what-if' transit and pedestrianization scenarios directly into Swiss direct-democracy public consultations.
key_democratic_safeguard: Open data and open-source agent-based transport code enabling independent verification prior to municipal votes.

hard_data_layers: Metropolitan 3D GIS, micro-climate heat models, transit corridor construction staging
soft_civic_layers: Neighborhood council workshops, street-corner public space redesign feedback loops
primary_civic_application: Turning passive neighborhood residents into co-designers of local public plazas and micro-climate interventions.
key_democratic_safeguard: Built on open-source web-GIS standards governed by the metropolitan public authority.

governance_model: Metropolitan Open Portal + Citizen Accessibility Crowdsourcing
hard_data_layers: 605-km2 citywide 3D twin, real-time wind corridors, solar radiation, fine-dust dispersion
soft_civic_layers: Crowdsourced wheelchair/elderly accessibility barriers (broken curbs, steep ramps, elevator outages)
primary_civic_application: Allowing citizens to test solar/shadow impacts on their own apartments and crowdsource disability mobility barriers.
key_democratic_safeguard: Universal browser/mobile access to high-compute environmental simulations previously restricted to developers.

project_name: 'Right to the Digital Twin City' & BPDA 3D Smart Model
lead_institutions: Boston Planning & Development Agency (BPDA), Boston University Civic Tech Researchers
hard_data_layers: Citywide 3D zoning & shadow model, urban heat island thermal layers, parcel redevelopment pipelines
soft_civic_layers: Community garden shadow audits, redlining historical overlays, Roxbury/Dorchester neighborhood testimony
primary_civic_application: Neighborhood advocates use 3D shadow and thermal models to contest zoning variances that threaten community gardens in historically redlined neighborhoods.
key_democratic_safeguard: Shifts 3D modeling from a closed planning-department tool into an adversarial public-hearing accountability instrument.

project_name: EPB Public Fiber Mobility & Road-Diet Twin
lead_institutions: City of Chattanooga, EPB Municipal Fiber Utility, UT Chattanooga (CUIP)
governance_model: Public Utility Infrastructure + Community Mobility Simulation
hard_data_layers: Municipally owned gigabit fiber telemetry, corridor traffic sensors, pedestrian safety & crash geometry
soft_civic_layers: Public transit rider feedback, pedestrian safety consultations (e.g., Frazier Avenue road diet)
primary_civic_application: Using municipal fiber telemetry to test 'road diet' configurations, protected bike lanes, and pedestrian safety alongside residents.
key_democratic_safeguard: Anchored on municipally owned public broadband infrastructure (EPB) rather than privatized telecom data enclosures.
